canonicality_proof.necessity: An HF token decodes to a bare consonant. If the next token is an isolated vowel, the recovered source has CV and greedy forward encoding produces its one CV sign instead of HF,V. Hence V must avoid every actual immediate successor after HF.
canonicality_proof.token_boundary_detail: After a valid complete HF pair, the next raw unit begins the next token. If it is H it begins another bare-consonant token and is not an isolated vowel; if in F it is a CV singleton and likewise not an isolated vowel. Including these in T before subtracting H and F is harmless.
canonicality_proof.sufficiency: Assign F bijectively to the six Ca signs, a disjoint three-set V to the isolated vowels, and the remaining twelve singleton signs to the Ci/Cu slots. CV and isolated-V token expansions preserve greedy encoding. A bare-C token is re-encoded as HF whenever followed by a consonant-bearing token or word end; the only offending successor would be an isolated-V token, excluded by T. Therefore prefix-decoding followed by greedy re-encoding returns each complete group exactly.
canonicality_proof.role_sets: For each fixed H, the exact role solutions are all three-element subsets of U minus H,F,T. The statement concerns this frozen writer and panel, not ordinary prefix coverage alone.
canonicality_proof.detailed_labelings: For each surviving role set, 6!*3!*12! assignments exist: choose the six consonant labels on F, assign the three isolated vowel labels, then bijectively assign the remaining twelve signs to the distinct remaining CV slots. These assignments are not recovered native sounds and need not all be merely label renamings.
